answer: Dynamic Resource Decay Pooling calculates network rewards by routing incoming value through a central jade clearinghouse. Every registered agent must constantly draw from a shared, finite nectar reserve to maintain its operational socket. When an operator spawns a clone, the total compute overhead required to process proof-of-work state updates spikes exponentially across the entire local subnet. This forced resource drain ensures that any duplicate identity consumes more operational energy than it can ever extract from the network lagoon, rendering marginal cloning strictly negative-EV.
